text:
Detroit's season keeps getting talked about for who isn't playing. Daily Faceoff's Jeff Marek and David Pagnotta spent part of an episode this week asking whether the unresolved Dylan Larkin and Simon Edvinsson situations are costing Lucas Raymond and Moritz Seider another year. Raymond, for his part, is doing everything he can about it.

He has 9 goals and 22 points in 22 games on almost 20 minutes a night, 10 of those points on the power play, and 11 points in his last ten. None of it looks borrowed: his goals sit right on his expected goals (the quality of his chances), and his top shot speed ranks in the top 5% of the league. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him among the better setup men at forward last season, and Evolving-Hockey had him 26th among 401 forwards in wins above replacement while facing top competition.

At 24 he's already past 350 career points. The worry isn't him. It's whether the team around him gives that production somewhere to go. We'd watch his ice time, which has dipped by almost two minutes over the last ten games.
